question.text: Scenario: Arun Kumar is analyzing Reliance Industries (RIL) stock using multiple technical indicators. Current observations: (1) RIL CMP: Rs.2,850. (2) 50-day SMA: Rs.2,780 (rising). 200-day SMA: Rs.2,650 (rising). (3) The 50-day SMA crossed above the 200-day SMA one month ago. (4) RSI: 58. (5) Bollinger Bands: Upper band Rs.2,950, Middle band Rs.2,780, Lower band Rs.2,610. Price is between middle and upper band. (6) Strong support at Rs.2,600 (tested 3 times in last 6 months). (7) Resistance at Rs.2,950 (tested twice). (8) Volume has been above average on recent up-days. (9) MACD is above the signal line and above the zero baseline. Question 1 of 5: The 50-day SMA crossing above the 200-day SMA one month ago is called:

answer.text: Golden cross — a bullish signal confirming the uptrend

explanation.text: The Logic: When a shorter-term moving average (here the 50-day SMA) crosses above a longer-term moving average (the 200-day SMA), the event is widely known as a "Golden Cross". It is interpreted as a bullish trend-confirmation signal because it shows that recent momentum has improved enough to pull the shorter average above the longer one. The opposite crossover — short-term MA crossing below the long-term MA — is called the "Death Cross" and is treated as bearish. The Trap: Calling this a Death Cross reverses the meaning — Death Cross is 50-day below 200-day, not above. "Silver cross" and "iron cross" are not standard technical-analysis terms in this context; they are distractors. Note: The Golden Cross / Death Cross terminology for a 50-day SMA crossing the 200-day SMA is not explicitly used or defined on the cited NISM Series XV Research Analyst pages checked (pp.295-327, including pp.300 and 317, which discuss moving-average crossovers and trend alignment generally). The terminology above reflects general industry technical-analysis usage rather than the cited workbook chapter.
